item.title: New York Deploys $360 Million for Stony Brook and Regional Hubs Supported by $1.37B in Federal Foundry Commitments
item.description:
New York State is investing $360 million in quantum technology, with $300 million for a Quantum Research and Innovation Hub at SUNY Stony Brook and $60 million for regional commercialization hubs. This initiative, supported by $1.37 billion in federal funding, aims to connect the state's hardware and semiconductor assets with enterprise demand in various sectors. The investment will establish open-access test facilities, foster startup incubation, and link regional hardware clusters with commercial end-users.

item.title: Review Unpacks China’s Surging Neutral-Atom Ecosystem: World-Record Arrays, Commercial Systems, and Scaling Milestones
item.description:
A review of China's neutral-atom quantum computing ecosystem reveals rapid advancements in hardware, including world-record atom trapping, high-fidelity gates, and commercial systems. While China leads in physical parameters and domestic supply chains, it lags behind Western efforts in system-level quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computing. The focus for China's roadmap is bridging the gap between physical demonstrations and continuous, fault-tolerant logical computation.

The post Review Unpacks China’s Surging Neutral-Atom Ecosystem: World-Record Arrays, Commercial Systems, and Scaling Milestones appeared first on Quantum Computing Report.
